title: Enamel Kiln
pages: Craft the controller from bricks, a solar tempered plate from the Solar Smelter, two Rhenium Filaments from the Wire Drawing Bench, a Thermocouple Probe and sealed steel plate. Place a lava cauldron directly beneath it. Build two courses of brick immediately east and west, and two blocks north and south (eight brick blocks total), then put iron bars on top of the north and south brick columns. Leave the blocks immediately north and south of the controller open for item ports. Keep the space over the controller open as the exhaust throat. Any missing upper brick or bar prevents firing. It is a tier-5 device: its Heliograph Plate replaces the daylight detector in the Heliostat Etcher recipe.

The probe senses the kiln's hot zone. Craft two Thermocouple Leg Pairs from four nickel ingots, one chromium ingot, one aluminum ingot and a Sealed Steel Plate; ingot tags accept other mods' matching metals. The Copper Hot Press joins one pair into a sheathed Thermocouple Probe over 200 ticks at 12 FE/t. Nickel/chromium and nickel/aluminum legs follow the Type K thermocouple material pairing, simplified for this game. A plain cauldron cannot replace the probe in the controller. The press takes item input from above or sides, FE through its capability, and offers output below; configure faces in its menu.

Hold the base batch in your main hand and one colorant ingot in your off hand, then right-click the formed controller. A full base batch and one ingot load into the kiln; each firing takes 40 ticks. Right-click with an empty hand afterward to collect the output, dropping any overflow. Incomplete batches are not accepted. The kiln will not fire with an empty or water-filled cauldron or with an incomplete flue; an empty off hand only shows a hint. Colorants are item tags (forge:ingots/<metal>), so any mod's matching ingot works.

It runs 20 datapack enameling recipes, each with a different metal. A daylight detector and rhenium make the Heliograph Plate. Three clay balls and tin make a bucket; four bricks and zirconium a cauldron; a chest and zinc a hopper; a furnace and tungsten a blast furnace; a blaze rod and antimony a brewing stand. Three stone and niobium make a stonecutter; four planks and hafnium a smithing table; six planks and molybdenum a shield. Three gold ingots and bismuth cast a bell, which otherwise cannot be crafted. Three copper ingots and gallium make a minecart; a minecart and palladium a hopper minecart. Four sticks and thallium make 16 rails; two sticks and indium two tripwire hooks. A wooden door with lead or a wooden trapdoor with cobalt becomes the iron version. Two flints and manganese make shears, one flint and aluminum flint and steel, four iron nuggets and vanadium two chains, and chiseled stone bricks with iridium a lodestone.

Automation: insert base items into slot 0 and colorant ingots into slot 1 from the north face. Sneak-click with an empty hand to cycle the south face to output, then extract the fired product there. A formed kiln processes a batch every 40 ticks; missing colorant or a broken flue pauses it without consuming stored items. Both slots and the face setting survive save/load. When two recipes match, the lowest recipe id wins. Refill the lava cauldron with a lava bucket; firing does not drain it. JEI lists base counts, colorant tags and outputs, with the kiln as catalyst.
